conviction_note: Near zero. The evidence leans slightly toward a revenue shortfall: the ~$53-55M consensus extrapolates a Q2 that included catch-up on Q1's stuck APU/landing-gear work orders, and Honeywell's Q3 aftermarket grew only 2% because of mechanical-parts constraints. Against that, 9.7% of shares are short at 9.4 days to cover, the stock sits 1.5% above its 52-week low after falling ~19% since mid-August, and this name rose 4.9% on its Q1 miss. So p_up 47 on abs 5.5 gives -0.33. The findings sum to +0.1, which differs in sign from the scaled number only because both are effectively zero. The squeeze and positive offsets are filed at full size, while p_up carries the slight fundamental lean.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue about $52.7M (Benzinga, mid-October per search snippet), $54M average of 5 analysts (Stockalarm snippet) and $55M (Tickflow). Q3 EPS is $0.43 (Benzinga) to $0.48 (Tickflow). The company gives no numeric guidance (Q2 6-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000808439/000117891326003832/zk2635845.htm). The aggregators roughly agree on revenue ($52.7-55M) and diverge on EPS. None was fetchable directly (403/sign-in), so the bar is snippet-sourced and every finding is capped small. Prior-year Q3 2025 revenue was $46.2M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/808439/000117891325003778/exhibit_99-1.htm). Q2 2026 actuals were $52.9M revenue and $0.35 adjusted EPS, against $44.9M / $0.30 expected.
positioning_check: FINRA short interest was 1,256,416 shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, 9.41 days to cover. Earlier settlements: 1,333,220 on 09-30 (10.78 days), 1,496,347 on 09-15 (13.63 days, the peak) and 1,395,853 on 08-31 (https://equibles.com/stocks/tatt/shortinterest). That is about 9.7% of 12.998M shares outstanding (Q2 6-K), and float is smaller, so this is a crowded short for a ~$3.7M/day name that has been covering modestly since mid-September. The stock has no options market (baseline: no_options_market), so there is no skew. The tape shows spot $32.00, 20-day run-up -9.07%, 5-day +1.11%, 47.6% below the 52-week high and 1.5% above the 52-week low. AAII (2026-10-30) reports one analyst downgrade in the past month and none upgrading, with the stock -3.67% intraday on 10-30.

findings.finding: The Q3 revenue bar (~$52.7-55M, versus $46.2M in Q3 2025, so +14-19% y/y) annualises Q2's $52.9M. Q2 included catch-up: Q1 ended with ~$15.5M of APU and landing-gear open work orders stuck for parts, and H1 revenue averaged $47M a quarter (Q1 $41.1M, Q2 $52.9M). Freedom Broker wrote on 2026-08-11 that 'such a high growth pace should not be expected to repeat in the coming quarters'. At ~+10-12% y/y, Q3 would print ~$51-52M, a 2-5% revenue miss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Confirmed prints only (the baseline history is polluted by AGM/proxy/contract 6-Ks). Q4 2025 (2026-03-18) missed revenue and EPS: -4% in extended trading (Seeking Alpha headline). Q1 2026 (2026-05-20) missed revenue ($41.1M vs $44.2M) and EPS ($0.26 vs $0.31) and the stock rose 4.93% on backlog (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/tat-technologies-shares-gain-despite-124609995.html). Q2 2026 (2026-08-05) beat revenue by 18% and closed +2.33% (baseline). The reaction to the revenue line is inconsistent, and the market has looked through misses when backlog grew.
findings.why_not_priced: Aggregator consensus moved up toward $54-55M after Q2 rather than settling near the H1 run-rate, so the estimates themselves have not absorbed the catch-up. Had the market fully priced a step-down, sell-side numbers would sit near ~$50-51M. The 19% fall from $39.6 (2026-08-11) to $32 and the 52-week-low price say a good part of the disappointment risk is already in the tape.
findings.independence: Q1 open-work-order figure and CFO timing ('resolved by the second half'): Q1 call coverage (https://www.barchart.com/story/news/2065561/tat-technologies-q1-earnings-call-highlights). Q1/Q2 revenue: TAT's own Q2 6-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000808439/000117891326003832/zk2635845.htm). The Q2 6-K also says supply conditions 'have not fully normalized'. Note: if 'dozens of APUs still awaiting parts' at Q2-end shipped in Q3, the same mechanism could lift Q3 instead, which is why the range runs positive.

findings.finding: Honeywell Aerospace, TAT's APU OEM, licensor and now parts supplier, reported Q3 2026 commercial aftermarket sales up only 2% organic ($2,126M vs $2,084M) on 2026-10-28, 'limited by mechanical component availability'. That is down from +8% in Q2. So the commodity/mechanical spares that stalled TAT's APU overhauls in Q1 stayed constrained through Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 parts-driven revenue decline (-2.4% y/y) was bought +4.93%, so a parts excuse has not been punished on this name before.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Honeywell already guided H2 aftermarket to low-to-mid single digits on mechanical supply on 2026-08-05 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002089271/000208927126000020/exhibit991q22026earningsre.htm). The Q3 confirmation at the low end came after TAT's last communication, and no TAT estimate visibly moved down for it. It is a proxy: TAT has not confirmed a Q3 parts shortfall. It lands on the MRO for aviation components segment ($27.7M of $52.9M in Q2). The heat-transfer OEM/MRO segments (~$23M) and engine coating are not APU-parts dependent, so the finding is sized net of them.
findings.independence: Honeywell's own Q2 release and 10-Q describe the same mechanical constraint (castings, forgings, bearings), so this is one supplier's statement seen twice and is counted once. Different source: TAT's Q2 6-K says supply chain conditions 'have not fully normalized' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000808439/000117891326003832/zk2635845.htm).

findings.finding: Short interest is 1.26M shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, ~9.7% of shares outstanding (more of float), at 9.41 days to cover, on a name sitting 1.5% above its 52-week low after -19% since mid-August. Shorts have trimmed from 1.50M (09-15), so the setup leans toward a squeeze on any non-disaster print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On Q1 2026, with a revenue and EPS miss, the stock rose 4.93%, which is consistent with positioning absorbing bad numbers.
findings.why_not_priced: The squeeze is a mechanism, not a price level. Nearly 9-10 days of volume must be bought back at ~116k shares/day, so a print that is merely in line can move the stock disproportionately. If the short were already covered, short interest would have fallen toward the ~0.7M (6%) of June 2026.
findings.independence: June 2026 short interest of 715k shares / 6.0% of float / 3.1 days (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/tat-technologies-ltd-nasdaqtatt-short-interest-up-881-in-june-2026-07-01/) shows the short built since mid-year.

findings.finding: Q3 is the first full quarter of TAT as Honeywell's sole global authorized distributor of GTCP 331-200/250 APU spare parts, announced 2026-07-14, with the MRO license extended to 2036. Freedom Broker estimates roughly $5M of annual revenue (~$1.25M a quarter, ~2% of the bar), which may not all be in estimates.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The announcement day (2026-07-14) closed +4.56% (baseline history row).
findings.why_not_priced: Small and partly priced: the deal is public and was rewarded on announcement. What is new is the first quarter of revenue and any disclosure of its run-rate. Freedom Broker notes the company has not confirmed the $5M figure. It is also offset by the same parts constraint Honeywell reported.
findings.independence: The size estimate comes from https://fbroker.kz/en/news/51416-freedom-broker-analysts-see-35-upside-potential-in-tat-technologies-shares-en-2 (2026-08-11), the same document as finding 1 but a different fact.

findings.finding: Aftermarket demand stayed strong in the quarter: AAR (fiscal Q1 to 2026-08-31, reported 2026-09-28) grew sales 24% and Parts Supply 31%, and guided next quarter to +14-16%. The demand side of TAT's MRO business is not the constraint, and the $615M backlog/LTAs (from $580M) should keep growing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Backlog growth was the stated reason the stock rose on the Q1 2026 miss (+4.93%).
findings.why_not_priced: A peer's demand read is mostly priced and is a proxy. TAT's revenue limiter is parts supply, not demand, so transmission to the print runs mainly through backlog/LTA headlines.
findings.independence: Honeywell's Q2/Q3 releases describe 'healthy underlying demand' limited by supply (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002089271/000208927126000031/exhibit991q32026earningsre.htm). That is the same document as finding 2, and here only the demand half is used.

findings.finding: AAII's composite reports one analyst downgrade of TATT in the month to 2026-10-29 and no upgrades, with the stock -3.67% intraday on 2026-10-30 at $32.27. The firm is unnamed.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced; it happened before entry. It is filed because a pre-print downgrade could mean the sell-side bar is drifting down, which would lower the effective bar, while the stated consensus may be stale.
findings.independence: The AAII 2026-10-02 piece (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/526716-why-tat-technologies-ltd8217s-tatt-stock-is-down-544) also mentions one downgrade in the prior month and may be the same action.

baseline_tension: The slight negative lean agrees with the -9% 20-day run-up and the 52-week-low price rather than cutting against it, which means much of it is likely priced. The crowded short (9.4 days to cover) cuts the other way, so p_up sits just under 50.

Rule 9 (segment net): the Honeywell parts finding lands on the ~52% APU/landing-gear segment only, so -1.0 to -0.5
Rule 1 (Q1 miss was bought +4.9%, Q2 beat only +2.3%): p_up moved from 45 to 47, so the scaled number went from -0.55 to -0.33
